heading: Send events. Prove they arrived.
intro: Hooklane sits between your product's events and your customers' endpoints: subscriptions, signed deliveries, automatic retries with backoff, and a delivery log you can query. This reference documents the full v1 surface — four endpoints, JSON over HTTPS, no SDK required.
metaDescription: Reference documentation for the Hooklane v1 API: manage webhook subscriptions, query the delivery log, and build every request as a copyable curl command.

auth.intro: Every request is authenticated with a secret API key sent in the Authorization header. Keys are scoped per environment: hk_live_ keys touch production subscriptions, hk_test_ keys only ever deliver to test endpoints.
auth.note: Examples keep the key as a $HOOKLANE_API_KEY shell variable — export it once and every copied command works as-is. Your key stays in your terminal: this reference never asks for it and never sends a request.

faqs.question: Does the try-it panel call the API?
faqs.answer: No. The panel assembles a curl command from the endpoint definition and your inputs, and the copy button copies exactly what you see. Nothing is ever sent from this page — you stay in control of when and where the request runs.

faqs.question: Where do I get an API key?
faqs.answer: Keys are created in the Hooklane dashboard under Settings → API keys. Live keys start with hk_live_, test keys with hk_test_. The reference examples read the key from a $HOOKLANE_API_KEY shell variable, so export it once and every copied command works unchanged.

faqs.question: How are deliveries signed?
faqs.answer: Every delivery carries an X-Hooklane-Signature header: an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the subscription's signing secret (the whsec_ value returned when you create the subscription). Verify it before trusting a payload, and rotate the secret by recreating the subscription.

faqs.question: What happens when an endpoint is down?
faqs.answer: Hooklane retries failed deliveries with exponential backoff — eight attempts spread over roughly 24 hours. Each attempt is a row in the delivery log with the response code we saw, so GET /v1/deliveries?status=failed shows you exactly what still needs attention.

faqs.question: Can I test without touching production?
faqs.answer: Yes. Requests made with an hk_test_ key operate on an isolated set of subscriptions and deliveries. The API surface is identical, so every command in this reference behaves the same in test mode.
